techQuestion.ask: Wes asked how SSO works with the master password. Can you give me one answer for Tom and one for Wes?

plain.text: Each person unlocks LastPass with a password only they know, and LastPass doesn't store it. Passwords are scrambled on the person's own laptop before anything is saved, so LastPass's servers hold only scrambled data. Business includes sign-in through your identity provider, like Microsoft. Our engineer will confirm in writing exactly how that fits your setup before Thursday.

precise.text: Vault data is encrypted and decrypted on the device with AES-256. The key is derived from the master password with PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations, and one more iteration produces a separate value used for authentication. LastPass states the plaintext master password is not stored on its servers. Federated login is included on Business and Business Max.

techQuestion.gap: Not in the approved library: how federated login derives and stores the vault key. I won't guess. Sent to the SE team to answer from the LastPass technical whitepaper, and to PMM to add to the library.
